sample_unit: surgical consent forms (liver resection) from 7 institutions, rated by 7 specialists

links.outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified Korean consent forms (KReaD and Natmal scores)
links.effect: KReaD fell from 1777 (SD 28.47) to 1335.6 (SD 59.95), P<.001; Natmal from 1452.3 (SD 88.67) to 1245.3 (SD 96.96), P=.007. Sentence length and difficult word ratio decreased.
links.quote: Artificial intelligence-assisted editing significantly improved readability, reducing the KReaD score from 1777 (SD 28.47) to 1335.6 (SD 59.95) (P<.001) and the Natmal score from 1452.3 (SD 88.67) to 1245.3 (SD 96.96) (P=.007).

links.outcome: Specialist clinician review of LLM-edited consent forms for risk, benefit, alternative content quality
links.effect: Specialist review detected declines in risk description (β=-0.371; P=.01) and overall impression (β=-0.500; P=.03) after LLM editing; evaluators found no explicit omissions but perceived text as overly simplified.
links.quote: The linear mixed-effects model confirmed significant reductions in risk descriptions (β₁=-0.371; P=.01) and overall impression (β₁=-0.500; P=.03), suggesting potential omissions in critical safety information.

unlisted_practices: Using LLMs to simplify non-English surgical consent forms while checking preservation of risk disclosure content

screen.reason: Evaluates the capability and risks (readability vs. omission of risk content) of using ChatGPT-4o to simplify Korean surgical consent forms, evaluated offline by clinical specialists.
